invariants.name: normalized-scenario-weights
invariants.expected: all plausible scenarios have finite non-negative weights summing to one

invariants.name: scenario-complete-priors-utilities-likelihoods
invariants.expected: every scenario defines every hypothesis, action utility and candidate survey exactly once

invariants.name: effort-feasibility
invariants.expected: every candidate portfolio respects the fixed survey-effort budget

invariants.name: no-observation-option
invariants.expected: the empty portfolio is always considered and has zero net EVSI

invariants.name: nominal-maximin-regret-separation
invariants.expected: weighted mean EVSI, maximin net EVSI and minimax regret are calculated as separate objectives

invariants.name: scenario-order-invariance
invariants.expected: reordering scenarios or survey candidates does not alter policy semantics

invariants.name: finite-support-total-variation-dro
invariants.expected: worst-case expected net EVSI is computed by reweighting nominal scenario probabilities within each declared TV radius

invariants.name: tv-radius-boundary-equivalence
invariants.expected: radius 0 reproduces nominal weighted expected EVSI and radius 1 reproduces finite-scenario maximin

invariants.name: tv-ambiguity-monotonicity
invariants.expected: optimal worst-case expected value cannot increase as the TV ambiguity radius grows

invariants.name: lower-tail-cvar-frontier
invariants.expected: maximize weighted average net EVSI in the worst alpha probability mass, with alpha 1 reducing to nominal expectation

invariants.name: tail-mass-correctness
invariants.expected: scenario probability is split at the alpha boundary when required; normalized tail weights sum to one

negativeControls.mutation: Use scenario weights that do not sum to one.
negativeControls.reason: Weighted expectations are invalid without a normalized scenario distribution.

baselines: finite-support total-variation DRO at multiple radii
qualificationBoundary: Synthetic scenarios show decision-criterion behavior only. Real robustness requires pre-registered scenario envelopes grounded in independent survey/campaign evidence and stakeholder-approved utilities. Finite-support total variation protects only against reweighting the supplied scenarios, not omitted scenarios or continuous distribution shift.
